purpose: The production planner's own trace for the two real-planner browser turns, transcribed verbatim from the world log. Kept as its own file because the diagnostic lines are what make a DECLINE publishable, and because the world's log is no longer on disk (see provenance).

provenance.why_gone: The worlds tree was pruned by ANOTHER process while this case was in flight: backend/data/acceptance_worlds went from 20 worlds to 2 (only write_combined and write_verify_0928 survived) and d5_browser_edit was removed with its run dir, its code export and its log. `preview_stack.py down` does NOT delete a world (cmd_down only signals the two pids and stamps stopped_at), so this was not the driver's teardown. A rebuild was then refused by run_isolated with 'could not read the live dev database read-only (disk I/O error)' on backend/data/atom.db, so the case could not be repeated on a fresh world. The two driver artifacts carry the world, run dir, source_id, ports, canvas ids, execution ids and audit ids needed to attribute the result; these lines are the only copy of the planner trace.

diagnosis.question: Why does the production planner decline a plain canvas edit sent from the real composer?
diagnosis.answer: Not a provider failure, not a canvas-identity failure, not a schema-contract failure. On the identical request bytes the same turn reached the planner, the planner answered with a well-formed CanvasEditPlan in 0.9s, and the answer was a CONSISTENT decline. Every other stage behaved: the composer sent the right canvas id, type, page and content; the lifecycle reservation, the claim and the release all ran; the refusal was reported truthfully and nothing was written.
what_this_rules_out: composer dropped the canvas / posted to a generic session -- RULED OUT: the captured request carries context.canvas_id, canvas_type='email', current_page='/canvas/<id>' and the full canvas_content, byte for byte

the provider was unavailable -- RULED OUT: the structured-trace line proves a CanvasEditPlan came back in 0.9s (openrouter WAS benched for account-level credit exhaustion mid-turn, and BPC fell over to opencode-go; that is a routing event, not the cause)
the 6e34725c7 schema-boundary contract bug -- RULED OUT for this turn: no violation was logged, so the plan was consistent and the bounded repair was never reached
the patch could not be applied (a find/replace mismatch) -- RULED OUT as the cause: with no ops there was nothing to match, and the pinned run's identical op DID apply cleanly
diagnosis.what_remains: Either the model behind the unpinned route (opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash) or the _EDITOR_SYSTEM prompt/template shape makes this request read as 'not an edit'. Both are un-separated by this evidence, and separating them needs either the plan body (which the product does not log for a consistent decline) or a second pin. NOT substituted: no accepting plan, no shim, no stub was used to make the unpinned turn pass.
follow_ups_worth_doing: log the plan SHAPE for every canvas-edit plan, not only on a contract violation -- as it stands a clean decline is not quotable without a re-run
A/B the unpinned rung against deepseek/deepseek-flash on the same prompt bytes to attribute the decline to the model rather than the prompt
